label_source: City of Brussels Grand Place building snapshot
status: supplemental open-licence facade candidates; source descriptions are weak labels, not reviewer visual classifications
selection_note: Images were selected from the Commons house categories for whole-facade views; sculptural details, ornament close-ups and interior shots were excluded after visual inspection. House of the Dukes of Brabant block photographs were excluded because a single frame spans several City dataset records (Grand-Place 13-19) and cannot be attributed to one record. A second pass extended coverage to the three remaining buildings with usable open-licence imagery: the Town Hall (City Hall, Grand-Place 8), the King of Bavaria (Grand-Place 12A, whose Commons descriptions state the address explicitly) and the King's House (Grand-Place 29-33). The King of Bavaria series is dominated by ornament details, so only its facade-bearing frames were taken. Grand-Place 37 (The Oak) and the Grand-Place 13-19 Dukes of Brabant block still have no image: Commons holds only multi-house group views for those, which cannot be attributed to one City record. The Dukes of Brabant block is covered by whole-composition photographs keyed to its facade unit rather than to a single house, because Grand-Place 13-19 form one designed facade. Grand-Place 37 (The Oak) shares its unit with Grand-Place 36 (The Little Fox) and is therefore covered by that unit's images. A second pass added one further view for each of the five facade units that had only a single image, so that every unit has at least two views and can participate in building-level retrieval. Candidates were checked against the Brussels monument record on the file page and inspected visually; sculptural details were rejected.
